explanation_en: This expression means 'in other words' or 'that is to say'. It is used to rephrase, clarify, or simplify a statement. It is highly versatile, suitable for both formal and informal registers, and is grammatically followed directly by the clarifying noun phrase or clause without any special conjugation.

examples.en_text: The office will be closed on Friday; in other words, we have a long weekend.
examples.target_text: Le bureau sera fermé vendredi, autrement dit, nous avons un long week-end.

examples.en_text: Our expenses exceed our income; in other words, we need to save money.
examples.target_text: Nos dépenses dépassent nos revenus, autrement dit, nous devons faire des économies.

examples.en_text: He didn't call me back; in other words, he is not interested in the project.
examples.target_text: Il ne m'a pas rappelé, autrement dit, il n'est pas intéressé par le projet.

examples.en_text: You got the best grade in the class; in other words, your hard work paid off.
examples.target_text: Tu as obtenu la meilleure note de la classe, autrement dit, ton travail a payé.

examples.en_text: The train is canceled; in other words, we are going to have to take the bus.
examples.target_text: Le train est annulé, autrement dit, nous allons devoir prendre le bus.

examples.en_text: She refuses to eat meat; in other words, she is a vegetarian.
examples.target_text: Elle refuse de manger de la viande, autrement dit, elle est végétarienne.

explanation_en: A 'distingo' is a noun meaning a subtle distinction, often used in intellectual, legal, or formal debates. It comes from Latin scholastic philosophy and is typically used with verbs like 'faire' (faire un distingo). Note that the plural can be written 'distingos' or remain invariable as 'distingo' depending on the spelling standard used.

examples.en_text: It is sometimes difficult to make a distinction between professional and private life.
examples.target_text: Il est parfois difficile de faire le distingo entre la vie professionnelle et la vie privée.

examples.en_text: The law makes a very clear distinction between these two types of offenses.
examples.target_text: La loi fait un distingo très clair entre ces deux types d'infractions.

examples.en_text: I don't really make a distinction between these two brands; to me, they are equal.
examples.target_text: Je ne fais pas vraiment de distingo entre ces deux marques, pour moi elles se valent.

examples.en_text: Why do you make a distinction between his first book and the second? They are very similar.
examples.target_text: Pourquoi fais-tu un distingo entre son premier livre et le deuxième ? Ils sont très similaires.

examples.en_text: The director made a subtle distinction between short-term and long-term goals.
examples.target_text: Le directeur a établi un distingo subtil entre les objectifs à court terme et à long terme.

examples.en_text: Children sometimes have trouble making the distinction between dreams and reality.
examples.target_text: Les enfants ont parfois du mal à faire le distingo entre le rêve et la réalité.

explanation_en: This colloquial idiom translates to 'a whole bunch of', 'a whole lot of', or 'heaps of'. It is used to emphasize a large, often disorganized quantity of something, whether concrete objects or abstract concepts like ideas or problems. Because of its informal register, it should be avoided in highly formal writing, where 'une multitude de' or 'de nombreux' would be preferred.

examples.en_text: I found a whole bunch of old books in my grandparents' attic.
examples.target_text: J'ai trouvé tout un tas de vieux livres dans le grenier de mes grands-parents.

examples.en_text: I still have a whole bunch of things to do before I can go on vacation.
examples.target_text: J'ai encore tout un tas de choses à faire avant de pouvoir partir en vacances.

examples.en_text: He made up a whole bunch of excuses for not coming to my birthday party.
examples.target_text: Il a inventé tout un tas d'excuses pour ne pas venir à ma fête d'anniversaire.

examples.en_text: Children always ask themselves a whole bunch of questions about the world around them.
examples.target_text: Les enfants se posent toujours tout un tas de questions sur le monde qui les entoure.

examples.en_text: You can find a whole bunch of useful tips on this travel forum.
examples.target_text: On peut trouver tout un tas de conseils utiles sur ce forum de voyage.

examples.en_text: This new update created a whole bunch of problems on my computer.
examples.target_text: Cette nouvelle mise à jour a créé tout un tas de problèmes sur mon ordinateur.

explanation_en: This pronominal verb means 'to be set up', 'to be put in place', or 'to fall into place'. It is widely used to describe systems, organizations, habits, or processes that are starting to function or become established. Learners should remember that it is always conjugated with 'être' in compound tenses because it is a pronominal verb.

examples.en_text: Everything is falling into place for the party tonight.
examples.target_text: Tout se met en place pour la fête de ce soir.

examples.en_text: The new project was set up very quickly.
examples.target_text: Le nouveau projet s'est mis en place très rapidement.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, things will eventually fall into place.
examples.target_text: Ne t'inquiète pas, les choses vont finir par se mettre en place.

examples.en_text: The musicians are getting into position on the stage before the start of the concert.
examples.target_text: Les musiciens se mettent en place sur la scène avant le début du concert.

examples.en_text: New safety rules will be put in place starting Monday.
examples.target_text: De nouvelles règles de sécurité vont se mettre en place dès lundi.

examples.en_text: The new organization is gradually being set up in the company.
examples.target_text: La nouvelle organisation se met en place petit à petit dans l'entreprise.

explanation_en: This expression literally translates to 'arsonist firefighter' and refers to a hypocritical entity that creates a problem or crisis only to present themselves as the savior who will solve it. It is commonly used in political, economic, and social commentary to criticize double standards or manipulative behavior. It functions as a compound noun and takes an 's' on both words in the plural ('pompiers pyromanes').

examples.en_text: Our boss is playing the arsonist firefighter: he creates tension in the team and then offers to resolve the conflict.
examples.target_text: Notre chef joue au pompier pyromane : il crée des tensions dans l'équipe et propose ensuite de résoudre le conflit.

examples.en_text: The government is acting like an arsonist firefighter by cutting budgets before offering emergency aid.
examples.target_text: Le gouvernement se comporte en pompier pyromane en coupant les budgets avant de proposer des aides d'urgence.

examples.en_text: She loves playing the arsonist firefighter: she starts rumors and then comes to comfort you.
examples.target_text: Elle adore jouer au pompier pyromane : elle lance des rumeurs et vient ensuite te consoler.

examples.en_text: This consultant is a real arsonist firefighter; he deliberately complicates the situation so that we hire him again.
examples.target_text: Ce consultant est un vrai pompier pyromane ; il complique exprès la situation pour qu'on l'embauche à nouveau.

examples.en_text: Stop acting like an arsonist firefighter by provoking arguments only to make romantic apologies later.
examples.target_text: Arrête de faire le pompier pyromane en provoquant des disputes pour ensuite faire des excuses romantiques.

examples.en_text: The media sometimes act like arsonist firefighters by creating panic and then selling solutions.
examples.target_text: Les médias agissent parfois comme des pompiers pyromanes en créant de la panique pour ensuite vendre des solutions.

explanation_en: This prepositional phrase means 'below', 'short of', or 'on this side of' a certain threshold, standard, or physical limit. It is often paired with 'de' (en deçà de) when followed by a noun, but can stand alone as an adverb meaning 'below' or 'inferior'. It belongs to a formal or written register and is the antonym of 'au-delà' (beyond).

examples.en_text: His recent results are well below our expectations.
examples.target_text: Ses résultats récents sont bien en deçà de nos attentes.

examples.en_text: The total cost of the project remained below the initial budget.
examples.target_text: Le coût total du projet est resté en deçà du budget initial.

examples.en_text: Temperatures this month are below seasonal averages.
examples.target_text: Les températures de ce mois-ci sont en deçà des normales de saison.

examples.en_text: You have a lot of talent, but this work is below your capabilities.
examples.target_text: Tu as beaucoup de talent, mais ce travail est en deçà de tes capacités.

examples.en_text: The pollution level in this area is finally below the legal limit.
examples.target_text: Le niveau de pollution dans cette zone est enfin en deçà de la limite légale.

examples.en_text: The quality of service in this hotel was short of what was promised on their website.
examples.target_text: La qualité du service dans cet hôtel était en deçà de ce qui était promis sur leur site.

explanation_en: This figurative expression means 'as soon as one tries to scratch the surface' or 'dig deeper' to uncover the truth or hidden details of a situation. The verb 'gratter' (to scratch) is used here metaphorically to imply looking past superficial appearances. It is idiomatic and slightly informal, perfect for conversational or journalistic contexts when discussing investigations or critical analysis.

examples.en_text: This bill seems perfect, but as soon as you try to scratch the surface, you discover big problems.
examples.target_text: Ce projet de loi semble parfait, mais dès qu'on essaie de gratter, on découvre de gros problèmes.

examples.en_text: He seems very cold, but as soon as you try to scratch the surface a little, you discover a very sensitive person.
examples.target_text: Il a l'air très froid, mais dès qu'on essaie de gratter un peu, on découvre quelqu'un de très sensible.

examples.en_text: This job offer is too good to be true; as soon as you try to scratch the surface, you see that the salary is very low.
examples.target_text: Cette offre d'emploi est trop belle pour être vraie ; dès qu'on essaie de gratter, on voit que le salaire est très bas.

examples.en_text: The history of this old house is fascinating as soon as you try to scratch the surface of the past a little.
examples.target_text: L'histoire de cette vieille maison est fascinante dès qu'on essaie de gratter un peu le passé.

examples.en_text: This brand calls itself eco-friendly, but as soon as you try to scratch the surface, you realize it's just marketing.
examples.target_text: Cette marque se dit écologique, mais dès qu'on essaie de gratter, on se rend compte que c'est juste du marketing.

examples.en_text: The details of this agreement are vague, and as soon as I try to scratch the surface, nobody wants to answer me.
examples.target_text: Les détails de cet accord sont flous, et dès que j'essaie de gratter, personne ne veut me répondre.

explanation_en: This idiom means 'all the time', 'constantly', or 'day in and day out'. It carries a strong connotation of weariness, annoyance, or excess, implying that the action is repetitive and tedious. It is typically used with verbs of action or communication, such as 'répéter', 'râler' (to complain), or 'travailler'.

examples.en_text: My colleague complains about his job all the time, it's tiring.
examples.target_text: Mon collègue se plaint de son travail à longueur de temps, c'est fatigant.

examples.en_text: Teenagers look at their phones all the time nowadays.
examples.target_text: Les adolescents regardent leur téléphone à longueur de temps aujourd'hui.

examples.en_text: In this region, it rains constantly during autumn.
examples.target_text: Dans cette région, il pleut à longueur de temps pendant l'automne.

examples.en_text: She listens to the same song all the time, I know it by heart now.
examples.target_text: Elle écoute la même chanson à longueur de temps, je la connais par cœur maintenant.

examples.en_text: Our dog barks constantly as soon as there is noise outside.
examples.target_text: Notre chien aboie à longueur de temps dès qu'il y a du bruit dehors.

examples.en_text: You can't think about work all the time, you need to relax.
examples.target_text: Tu ne peux pas penser au travail à longueur de temps, tu as besoin de te détendre.

explanation_en: This extremely common expression means 'to have difficulty doing' or 'to struggle to do' something. It is always followed by an infinitive verb introduced by the preposition 'à' (avoir du mal à faire quelque chose). It is highly versatile, used across all registers of French, and is a more natural, everyday alternative to 'avoir des difficultés à'.

examples.en_text: I have difficulty sleeping when it's too hot.
examples.target_text: J'ai du mal à dormir quand il fait trop chaud.

examples.en_text: He struggles to understand his math teacher.
examples.target_text: Il a du mal à comprendre son professeur de mathématiques.

examples.en_text: We had a hard time finding the restaurant without a map.
examples.target_text: Nous avons eu du mal à trouver le restaurant sans plan.

examples.en_text: When I was a child, I had trouble reading.
examples.target_text: Quand j'étais enfant, j'avais du mal à lire.

examples.en_text: Do you have difficulty getting up early in the morning?
examples.target_text: Est-ce que vous avez du mal à vous lever tôt le matin ?

examples.en_text: They will have a hard time finishing this project on time.
examples.target_text: Ils auront du mal à finir ce projet à temps.

explanation_en: This expression translates to 'just in case,' 'for what it's worth,' or 'for any useful purpose.' It is commonly used in professional or formal contexts to provide extra information that might be helpful but isn't strictly requested. A common pitfall for learners is overusing it in highly casual speech, as it carries a slightly formal, administrative, or polite tone.

examples.en_text: I am sending you the summary of our meeting, just in case.
examples.target_text: Je vous envoie le récapitulatif de notre réunion, à toutes fins utiles.

examples.en_text: Here is my cell phone number, for whatever it's worth, in case you have any trouble this weekend.
examples.target_text: Voici mon numéro de portable, à toutes fins utiles, si jamais vous avez un problème ce week-end.

examples.en_text: I printed the plane tickets just in case, even though we already have them on our phones.
examples.target_text: J'ai imprimé les billets d'avion à toutes fins utiles, même si nous les avons déjà sur nos téléphones.

examples.en_text: For what it's worth, you should know that the museum is free on the first Sunday of the month.
examples.target_text: À toutes fins utiles, sachez que le musée est gratuit le premier dimanche du mois.

examples.en_text: I kept a copy of the old contract just in case.
examples.target_text: J'ai gardé une copie de l'ancien contrat à toutes fins utiles.

examples.en_text: I'm leaving you the address of the nearest clinic, just in case.
examples.target_text: Je te laisse l'adresse de la clinique la plus proche, à toutes fins utiles.

explanation_en: In this figurative sense, 'embarquer quelqu'un' means to captivate, engross, or sweep someone up in a story, idea, or project. It is a colloquial but widely accepted expression, often used when talking about books, movies, or persuasive pitches. Learners should note that in more formal registers, verbs like 'captiver' or 'transporter' are preferred, while the literal meaning of 'embarquer' is simply to board a vehicle or to involve someone in a tricky situation.

examples.en_text: This detective novel got me hooked from the very first chapter.
examples.target_text: Ce roman policier m'a embarqué dès le premier chapitre.

examples.en_text: The movie was a bit long, but the story completely swept me away.
examples.target_text: Le film était un peu long, mais l'histoire m'a complètement embarqué.

examples.en_text: From the very first notes, this melody swept me away to another world.
examples.target_text: Dès les premières notes, cette mélodie m'a embarqué dans un autre monde.

examples.en_text: When he told me about his start-up project, his enthusiasm got me hooked right away.
examples.target_text: Quand il m'a parlé de son projet de start-up, son enthousiasme m'a tout de suite embarqué.

examples.en_text: The virtual art exhibition really swept me away; it was magical.
examples.target_text: L'exposition d'art virtuel m'a vraiment embarqué, c'était magique.

examples.en_text: She started telling her childhood memories, and her story swept me away.
examples.target_text: Elle a commencé à raconter ses souvenirs d'enfance et son récit m'a embarqué.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase means 'ultimately,' 'in the final analysis,' or 'lastly.' It is used to introduce the final point in an argument or to describe the ultimate state of something. It belongs to a formal or written register, and learners should avoid confusing it with 'en premier lieu' (in the first place) or using it in casual, everyday conversations where 'finalement' or 'en fin de compte' would sound more natural.

examples.en_text: After hesitating between several options, we ultimately chose to stay at home.
examples.target_text: Après avoir hésité entre plusieurs options, nous avons choisi, en dernier lieu, de rester à la maison.

examples.en_text: If you can't manage to fix the computer, contact technical support as a last resort.
examples.target_text: Si vous n'arrivez pas à réparer l'ordinateur, contactez le service technique en dernier lieu.

examples.en_text: We must think about the budget and, lastly, about the project's launch date.
examples.target_text: Nous devons penser au budget et, en dernier lieu, à la date de lancement du projet.

examples.en_text: The doctor advised me to change my diet and, as a last resort, to take medication.
examples.target_text: Le médecin m'a conseillé de changer de régime et, en dernier lieu, de prendre des médicaments.

examples.en_text: For our trip, we will visit Rome, Florence and, lastly, Venice.
examples.target_text: Pour notre voyage, nous visiterons Rome, Florence et, en dernier lieu, Venise.

examples.en_text: Ultimately, it is the director who will make the decision.
examples.target_text: C'est le directeur qui prendra la décision en dernier lieu.
